lead: The Gulf war came closer to Pakistan's new commitments as the Houthis claimed a strike near Riyadh and Saudi jets hit Sanaa, days before the Makkah pact's defence committee meets in the Saudi capital. With India, Islamabad and New Delhi traded formal protests over the two civilians killed near Kasur, while Pakistan pushed back at the UN over Kashmir and the suspended Indus Waters Treaty. On money, disrupted Qatari LNG is forcing a shift to costlier furnace oil for power, and a national goods transport strike threatens supply lines from 10 October.

stories.headline: Pakistan and India trade protests over Kasur border killings
stories.summary: Islamabad summoned India's chargé d'affaires, accusing the Border Security Force of using unprovoked lethal force against two unarmed civilians in the Bedian sector. New Delhi summoned a Pakistani diplomat in turn, saying the men had crossed illegally into Indian territory, Arab News reported.

stories.headline: Dar and British envoy review UK ties and regional situation
stories.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar met the UK's envoy to discuss bilateral relations, and the two sides exchanged views on the shifting regional picture, the Foreign Office said.

stories.headline: Houthis claim Riyadh strike as Saudi jets pound Sanaa
stories.summary: Fire and smoke were seen near an Aramco facility south of Riyadh after the Houthis claimed an attack, and Houthi-run media reported 26 Saudi strikes on Sanaa in reply; the Saudi-led coalition called the Houthi claims misleading. The escalation raises the stakes for Pakistan ahead of next week's Makkah pact defence committee meeting in Riyadh.

stories.headline: Eleven militants reported killed in KP and Balochistan
stories.summary: Security sources, quoted by state media, said 11 militants were killed in separate intelligence-based operations, including five in South Waziristan and others after an attack on a checkpost in Balochistan's Mashkel area. Officials described them as belonging to groups the state links to India; the claim could not be independently verified.

stories.headline: Punjab CTD says it arrested 13 suspects in a week
stories.summary: Punjab's Counter Terrorism Department said 98 intelligence-led operations this week led to 13 arrests from banned groups, including a man from Pakpattan it alleges was working for Indian intelligence.

stories.headline: Bilawal says Centre was set on emergency rule in KP
stories.summary: PPP chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said the federal government had decided to impose an emergency or governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, but his party pressed for a political route instead. He called for a joint Centre–province approach to counterterrorism and urged the KP government to put security first.

stories.headline: Disrupted Qatari LNG pushes power sector back to furnace oil
stories.summary: With LNG deliveries from Qatar disrupted by the Hormuz crisis, Pakistan is burning more furnace oil to meet peak evening demand, officials and analysts said. The choice is between pricier alternative fuels, expensive spot cargoes or load-shedding.

stories.headline: Goods transporters call nationwide strike from 10 October
stories.summary: The All-Pakistan Goods Transporters Association gave the government an ultimatum over its list of demands and announced a countrywide strike from 10 October. It comes as truckers already avoid routes north over fears of container seizures before the PTI march.

stories.headline: Karachi port one-stop centre fast-tracked as transshipment grows
stories.summary: Maritime Affairs Minister Junaid Anwar Chaudhry ordered faster work on a single-window facilitation centre for port businesses in Karachi, as Gulf disruption lifts transshipment through Pakistani ports.

stories.headline: Used-car imports jump after rules eased
stories.summary: Imports of second-hand cars rose sharply in September after the government relaxed import rules, drawing complaints from local assemblers; importers argue the change brings competition to a protected sector.

stories.headline: Fuel sales slip 2% year on year in September
stories.summary: Oil marketing companies sold 1.3 million tonnes in September, 2% less than a year earlier but 7% more than in August, Topline Research said, taking first-quarter FY27 volumes to 4.1 million tonnes.

stories.headline: KP has drawn nearly Rs800bn from war-on-terror share since 2010
stories.summary: Official data show Khyber Pakhtunkhwa received about Rs799bn under the extra 1% of the divisible pool granted for counterterrorism since 2010-11, a figure likely to feed the debate over provincial security spending and NFC shares.

stories.headline: KSE-100 ends week 1.5% lower on oil and US–Iran worries
stories.summary: The benchmark index lost 1.5% over the week as uncertainty over US–Iran relations and high oil prices kept investors cautious and average daily volumes fell.

stories.headline: Pakistan rejects India's 'internal matter' line on Kashmir at UN
stories.summary: In a right-of-reply exchange at the UN, Pakistan rejected India's description of Kashmir as an internal matter, saying the territory's final status remains unresolved under UN resolutions.

stories.headline: UN rights council side event warns on Indus treaty suspension
stories.summary: Speakers at an event on the sidelines of the UN Human Rights Council said India's decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance threatens water security, farming and livelihoods for millions across the Indus Basin.

stories.headline: Government–PTI talks end in deadlock as march begins
stories.summary: A second marathon round of talks broke up early on Sunday without agreement, leaving the PTI's march on Islamabad, set to start from southern KP today, on course.

stories.headline: Rangers deployment in Islamabad and Punjab extended to 15 October
stories.summary: The government approved keeping Rangers in the capital and parts of Punjab to back police during the PTI march.

stories.headline: Five killed in Ratodero shooting
stories.summary: Five people, including a passer-by, were killed in a shooting linked to a feud in Ratodero near Larkana, and the Sindh chief minister has ordered a report.

stories.headline: Freed tanker crew due home as bodies of three are repatriated
stories.summary: Four Pakistani sailors freed from Somali pirates are due in Karachi on Sunday, while the PMO said the remains of three crew killed in the rescue operation are being flown home.
